subject: SLA template: provisional availability exception & monthly credit roadmap
body:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@novatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novatech Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA template — request for provisional availability carveout

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning. Novatech is excited to move forward but procurement has flagged a couple of items in Redwood's standard SLA that are blockers for our legal team. The main asks:

- A provisional availability exception for the first 90 days post-production cutover (we expect testing/batched ramp might impact uptime % in that window).
- A cap on monthly service credits during that provisional window — procurement wants a fixed monthly ceiling rather than open-ended per-incident credits.
- Slightly relaxed latency SLO for batched inference routes (p95 from 120ms -> 200ms) while we tune our batching strategy.

Attached is the latest SOW (Novatech_SOW_draft_v2.pdf) with redlines. Can Redwood propose an operational roadmap that maps the provisional carveout to clear rollback/monitoring gates? Procurement also wants the monthly credit schedule baked into the DocuSign flow.

Appreciate a short proposal we can circulate with legal by end of next week.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Cloud Integrations
Novatech

---

On Wed, 26 Aug 2026 at 10:05 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template — request for provisional availability carveout

Hi Aisha — thanks for the details and the SOW. Two quick notes:

1) We can support a time-boxed provisional exception for the cutover period, but we need operational gates (health metrics) and an explicit mitigation plan to avoid open-ended credit exposure.
2) We prefer a credit cap expressed as a percentage of the monthly invoice or a fixed-dollar cap — both are doable.

I’ve looped in Marissa and Ben to propose the credit ladder and Laura for legal redlines.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to propose a 90-day provisional exception with explicit gate criteria (error budget consumption, regional latency breaches, KV cache warming thresholds).
- Draft monthly credit cap options (3 tiers) + example calculations for Novatech's expected run-rate.
- Legal to propose language for roll-forward/rollback and evidence requests.

We’ll circulate a short one-pager and an updated annotated SLA template by Thursday end of day. Does that timeline work?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template — provisional availability exception & monthly credit roadmap\n
Team — drafting the credit ladder and run-rate examples now. Early thoughts:

- Option A (Conservative): Fixed monthly cap = 10% of monthly committed spend during the 90-day window. Credits prorated by day and limited to cumulative 10% for period.
- Option B (Balanced): Fixed-dollar cap equal to 1.5x average expected monthly credits (we'll compute with Novatech numbers) — more predictable for Novatech but higher cap for Redwood.
- Option C (Operationally aligned): Rolling cap tied to incident severity (S1/S2/S3) with an absolute ceiling of $X/month (we'll run numbers).

Also proposing explicit gate metrics to sunset the provisional exception early if Novatech demonstrates stable p95 latency & availability for two consecutive 14-day windows.

Attachments: redwood-sla-template-annotated.docx (working copy)

Marissa
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@novatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template — provisional availability exception & monthly credit roadmap

Aisha — appreciate the clarity in the SOW. From a legal perspective, we can accept a provisional 90-day carveout provided: 

- The carveout is strictly timeboxed and terminates automatically unless both parties agree to an extension in writing.
- Redwood will provide weekly evidence packets (uptime/latency dashboards, incident timelines, cache-warm stats) during the provisional window.
- Credits are limited to the agreed cap and computed per the SLA formula in the template; no unilateral upfront offsets outside the DocuSign flow.

I’ve suggested tidy language in the attached annotated template (see section 4.2 — provisional exception). We should confirm DocuSign placeholders for the chosen cap and whether Novatech wants percentage vs fixed-dollar.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@novatech.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template — provisional availability exception & monthly credit roadmap

Thanks all — that helps. High-level preference from Novatech procurement/legal: fixed-dollar monthly cap (they want absolute predictability on financial exposure). Can you propose three fixed-dollar caps tied to our expected monthly committed spend? Also, can the gate for sunsetting be 14 days *stable* (rather than two *14-day windows*)?

We can share expected run-rate numbers if you need them to model options. Would like a one-pager and the annotated template returned so we can feed it into our DocuSign process next week.

Best,
Aisha

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@novatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA template — provisional availability exception & monthly credit roadmap

Aisha — attached is the one-pager and three fixed-dollar cap options modeled against two Novatech run-rate scenarios. Quick summary:

- Low-run-rate (expected $120k/mo): Caps = $6k / $12k / $24k (representing ~5% / 10% / 20% of committed spend).
- High-run-rate (expected $480k/mo): Caps = $24k / $48k / $96k.

Sunsetting gate: Redwood accepts a single 14-day stable window with the following acceptance criteria: avg p95 <= 180ms and availability >= 99.6% for the window. If met, the provisional carveout expires automatically and the standard SLA applies the next billing cycle.

I’ve included the annotated SLA with placeholders for the chosen cap and the DocuSign merge fields. If those numbers look OK I can upload to DocuSign and share the link for Novatech procurement to sign.

Attachments: Novatech_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (with margin notes), redwood-sla-template-annotated.docx, one-pager-credit-options.pdf

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

Notes: attachments referenced above are stubs in the thread. Internal participants handled all redlines and proposed operational gates; Novatech preferred fixed-dollar caps and a single 14-day stable gate.
